title: tune-nccl-overlap-kvcache-continuous-batching-tp-kernel-scheduling
author: Asha Patel
description: Context: Tensor-parallel multi-GPU workloads were seeing suboptimal overlap between NCCL collectives and device compute, and KV cache sharding + continuous batching introduced head-of-line latency in some p99 cases. Motivation: Improve throughput and tail latency for large-sequence TP models without changing model correctness. Goals: 1) increase overlap of communication and compute by adjusting stream priorities and non-blocking collectives, 2) introduce lighter-weight kernel scheduling heuristics to avoid unnecessary syncs, 3) shard KV cache access to reduce cross-device contention, and 4) modify continuous batching to reduce tail latencies for small queries while preserving batching efficiency for throughput workloads. Changes: - NCCL: introduced a configurable priority stream for collectives and a fall-back async path using ncclGroupStart/ncclGroupEnd to batch short-lived collectives; added checks to avoid implicit cudaDeviceSynchronize in the TP collective wrapper. - Streams/scheduling: reworked kernel dispatch to use per-TP-stage streams with explicit cudaStreamWaitEvent handoffs instead of global syncs; added heuristics that promote compute kernels to higher-priority streams when their dependent collectives are on low-priority streams, reducing serialization. - KV cache: implemented sharded KV lookup paths where keys are routed to owning device first, added lightweight local-cache for recent prefixes to reduce NCCL all-to-alls for common prefixes; introduced a per-request affinity hint to keep hot-key lookups colocated. - Continuous batching: added a dynamic flush policy that uses recent latency histograms to prefer earlier flush for low-latency single-request workloads; added a per-model sequence-length threshold that bypasses batching for very short requests in latency-critical routes. - Tests/bench: unit tests for TP collective ordering, integration tests against emulated 4xA100 cluster in perf-lab, microbenchmarks comparing baseline to optimized code paths. Results: internal perf runs show 12-18% throughput improvement on TP4-32k-like models at batch sizes typical for Dedicated customers, with p99 latency reduction up to 20% on mixed short/long workloads and up to 2x reduction in KV-related NCCL traffic for common prefix workloads. Backwards compatibility: behavior is guarded behind config flags (runtime.tpu.tp_nccl_overlap_opt and runtime.kvcache.sharded_lookup) and defaults to off for on-prem private installs until validated. Implementation notes: kept changes localized to serving/runtime/tp and serving/runtime/kvcache to minimize surface area; new flags exposed in config proto and Redwood Console. Checklist: implemented, unit-tested, added perf benchmarks, added release notes, documented config flags. Impact: no API changes; operator-visible config documented.
commits: 1) initial refactor of TP collective wrappers and stream abstraction; 2) add NCCL priority stream support and async group path; 3) implement sharded KV lookup and local prefix cache; 4) add continuous-batching dynamic flush heuristics and config knobs; 5) tests and perf benchmarks; 6) docs and release notes
files_changed: serving/runtime/tp/collectives.cc (rework collective wrapper, add ncclGroupStart path, avoid implicit syncs), serving/runtime/tp/stream_scheduler.h/.cc (introduce per-stage streams and priority heuristics), serving/runtime/kvcache/sharded_lookup.cc (shard routing + local prefix cache), serving/runtime/batching/continuous_batcher.cc (dynamic flush policy), proto/config/runtime.proto (new flags), tests/perf/tp_nccl_overlap_perf.py (bench harness), tests/unit/tp_collective_ordering_test.cc, docs/ops/nn/perf_tuning.md (how to enable flags), console/ui/config-schema.json
review_conversation: Marta: Nice work, measurable numbers are convincing. Asha: Thanks, most numbers are from 4xA100 perf-lab runs, see attached benchmarks. Liam: One concern: are we sure the async ncclGroup path doesn't regress small-batch latency? Can we gate it? Asha: gated behind runtime.tpu.tp_nccl_overlap_opt and fallback to sync for batch_size<=2; also added canary in Dedicated rollout. Samir: KV sharding introduces routing overhead - do we have CPU cost numbers? Asha: microbench shows ~3% CPU increase for request path but NCCL traffic drop gives net latency improvement; added optimization to avoid routing for very short prefixes. Marta: Please add a note in docs about operator flags and default off for Private. Asha: Added docs and config proto. Liam: CI flaky test on windows runner failed once, re-ran and passed. Approvals: Liam approved, Marta approved, Samir approved.
release_notes: Improved multi-GPU tensor-parallel performance: NCCL stream priorities and async group collectives to increase comm/compute overlap; sharded KV cache lookups and local prefix cache to reduce cross-device traffic; continuous-batching dynamic flush policy to improve p99 for mixed workloads. Feature is behind runtime flags; operators should validate in staging before enabling in Private installs.
